survey: A folding camp armchair seen in three-quarter view from the front left. Green fabric covers the seat and backrest, with a raised lime edge, and a tent-and-campfire logo is printed on the back. Two grey vertical back posts run from the top corners of the backrest down to the ground. The seat hangs between four clips. At the two front clips, the tops of a front X-brace meet the bottoms of slanted armrest posts. The X-brace pivots on a single bolt below the seat. Each padded armrest rests on its front post, and its back end sits against the backrest post. The chair stands on capped feet: three are visible, and the back right foot is hidden or unclear. There is no cross-bracing on the sides or at the back. The frame is nearly the same as the one in example 2, which the reviewer marked major.

errors.where: Frame below the seat: front X-brace, side and back legs
errors.what: The frame does not add up. The only scissor mechanism is one X across the front. Its upper ends end at the seat's front clips, and the armrest posts start at the same clips. The back legs are straight rigid posts with no cross-bracing on the sides or back. In a real folding chair the legs make an X on each side, or front and back, joined by hinged seat rails. This frame has no joints that would let it fold. It also has nothing on the sides to stop it racking sideways, so it could neither fold nor stand firmly.

errors.where: Front seat corners, where the X-legs, armrest posts and seat clips meet
errors.what: Three tubes join at one fabric clip with no hinge or tube joint. The X-leg ends at the clip, and the armrest post rises from the same point at a different angle. Fabric clips cannot carry leg or armrest loads.
The back right leg and foot are not clearly shown. Only three feet can be read for certain, so it is unclear what holds up the back right corner.

fix: Folding camp armchair with a correct scissor frame: on each side, two tubes cross in an X joined by a pivot bolt. The front and back legs join at the top through horizontal seat rails along the fabric edges. Armrest posts rise from the seat rails at real tube joints, not from fabric clips. Back posts continue up from the back legs to hold the backrest. Four legs, each with a visible foot cap, all resting on the ground.
